scenario: AITA for lying to my bf and letting him believe his ex cheated on him? | I know this sounds really bad but just hear me out. it's been eating me up inside so I'd like some feedback. We're currently college seniors and we started dating only 4 months ago. For his first two years he was dating another girl that I somewhat knew since we're in the same sorority but I wasn't close to. I had a crush on him since basically freshman year but I knew he was dating this girl. Anyways they ultimately broke up because he suspected she was cheating due to rumors about a party where she reportedly danced and kissed some guy. I was also there but I don't remember seeing her since it was a huge venue that was hosted by our sorority and we didn't really have overlapping friends circles. So when we started dating he was obviously still really torn up about his ex and questioning their break-up. It really stung to see him still so torn up about it, since all I wanted for us was a new start and for him to forget his ex completely. So when he asked me if I had seen his ex at that party, I don't know why but I lied and said that I had seen her with other guys. That really sealed it for him and I think he's moved on a lot faster. He says it's a no-brainer that they broke up because she cheated and now he knows for sure. He says he feels a lot better knowing that he didn't dump her for no reason. I know there's nothing to gain by telling the truth now. He's so much happier than before and he has no regrets about his exgf anymore. So, am I the asshole for lying and keeping up with the lie?

However, this is a gray area, and the potential consequences should be carefully weighed. 2. **Intent vs. Impact** – Your intent was to help your boyfriend move on and avoid further pain. While your motivation was compassionate, the act of lying—even with good intentions—can erode trust over time. Trust is fragile, and once broken, it can take a long time to rebuild. 4. **Alternative Approaches** – Instead of lying, you could have: - Acknowledged that you weren’t sure what happened at the party (since you didn’t actually see her). - Reassured him that his feelings were valid, regardless of what others might have done. - Focused on building his confidence in your relationship rather than undermining his ex’s reputation. 5. **Relationship Dynamics** – You’re in a relatively new relationship (4 months), and he’s still processing a past breakup. While it’s understandable to want to "fix" his pain, relationships thrive on mutual respect and transparency. Here’s why: - **Trust is non-negotiable.** A relationship built on lies, even small ones, is fundamentally unstable. - **You’re not his therapist.** It’s not your job to "fix" his ex’s reputation or his feelings about her. Acknowledge that lying wasn’t the solution. 2. **Reaffirm your commitment to honesty.** If you’ve been lying about this, be transparent with him now—even if it means admitting you lied. Own it, apologize, and explain why you did it. This shows growth and integrity. 3. **Focus on building your relationship on truth.** Moving forward, prioritize open communication. If he asks about his ex again, be honest: *"I wasn’t there, so I don’t know what happened. But I believe you when you say you’re over it."* 4. **Address the root issue.** If you’re still struggling with seeing him hurt, work on processing your own feelings (e.g., why his ex’s actions bothered you so much) rather than trying to control his emotions. ### **Final Thought:** You’re not a bad person for caring about him, but lying—even with good intentions—is a moral failure. The fact that you’re questioning this shows you’re capable of recognizing the wrong in what you did. The next step is to repair the trust by being honest, even if it’s uncomfortable.
